claim: The ability to distinguish males from females is essential for productive mate selection and species propagation.
source: The ability to distinguish males from females is essential for productive mate selection and species propagation.
evidence: This is a general statement about biological reproduction that draws from established scientific understanding.

claim: Recent studies in Drosophila have identified different classes of contact chemosensory neurons that detect female or male pheromones and influence courtship decisions.
source: Recent studies in Drosophila have identified different classes of contact chemosensory neurons that detect female or male pheromones and influence courtship decisions.
evidence: This statement references prior research findings in the field.

claim: Sensory neurons that detect female pheromones, but not male pheromones, activate a novel class of neurons in the ventral nerve cord to cause activation of P1 neurons.
source: We find that sensory neurons that detect female pheromones, but not male pheromones, activate a novel class of neurons in the ventral nerve cord to cause activation of P1 neurons, male-specific command neurons that trigger courtship.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by calcium imaging and optogenetic experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: P1 neurons are male-specific command neurons that trigger courtship.
source: We find that sensory neurons that detect female pheromones, but not male pheromones, activate a novel class of neurons in the ventral nerve cord to cause activation of P1 neurons, male-specific command neurons that trigger courtship.
evidence: This characterization of P1 neurons is based on established knowledge from prior studies.

claim: Sensory neurons that detect male pheromones activate central mAL neurons to inhibit P1.
source: In addition, sensory neurons that detect male pheromones, as well as those that detect female pheromones, activate central mAL neurons to inhibit P1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by calcium imaging and behavioral experiments in the manuscript.

claim: Sensory neurons that detect female pheromones activate central mAL neurons to inhibit P1.
source: In addition, sensory neurons that detect male pheromones, as well as those that detect female pheromones, activate central mAL neurons to inhibit P1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by calcium imaging experiments in the manuscript.

claim: The balance of excitatory and inhibitory drives onto central courtship-promoting neurons controls mating decisions.
source: These studies demonstrate that the balance of excitatory and inhibitory drives onto central courtship-promoting neurons controls mating decisions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Male Drosophila follow, sing to, and copulate with females but not males.
source: The specificity of mating decisions is exemplified by the Drosophila courtship ritual, in which males follow, sing to, and copulate with females but not males.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila courtship behavior.

claim: A male-specific splice form of the Fruitless transcriptional regulator (FruM) is expressed in peripheral and central neurons that drive courtship behavior.
source: A major advance in elucidating the neural circuits that govern male mating decisions has come from the discovery that a male-specific splice form of the Fruitless trancriptional regulator (FruM) is expressed in peripheral and central neurons that drive courtship behavior (Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005), arguing that FruM marks neural circuits for courtship.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: FruM marks neural circuits for courtship.
source: A major advance in elucidating the neural circuits that govern male mating decisions has come from the discovery that a male-specific splice form of the Fruitless trancriptional regulator (FruM) is expressed in peripheral and central neurons that drive courtship behavior (Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005), arguing that FruM marks neural circuits for courtship.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern of FruM and cited research.

claim: Studies of the function of FruM-positive neurons has led to the identification of olfactory and gustatory neurons that detect pheromones, as well as central neurons that drive behavioral subprograms of courtship.
source: Studies of the function of FruM-positive neurons has led to the identification of olfactory and gustatory neurons that detect pheromones, as well as central neurons that drive behavioral subprograms of courtship (Datta et al., 2008; Ha and Smith, 2006; Kurtovic et al., 2007; Lu et al., 2012; Ruta et al., 2010; Thistle et al., 2012; Toda et al., 2012; von Philipsborn et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement summarizes findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: P1 neurons are located in the protocerebrum.
source: One set of neurons that has emerged as a central driver of male mating behavior is the group of P1 (a.k.a. pMPe, pMP4 or pC1) neurons in the protocerebrum (Cachero et al., 2010; Kimura et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2002; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Inducible activation of P1 neurons leads to sustained male courtship behaviors.
source: Inducible activation of these neurons leads to sustained male courtship behaviors (Inagaki et al., 2014; Kohatsu et al., 2011; Pan et al., 2012; von Philipsborn et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: P1 neurons are activated by female pheromones.
source: Moreover, these neurons are activated by female pheromones and this activation is partially inhibited in the presence of the male inhibitory pheromone, cis vaccenyl actate (cVA) (Kohatsu et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: P1 neuron activation is partially inhibited in the presence of the male inhibitory pheromone, cis vaccenyl acetate (cVA).
source: Moreover, these neurons are activated by female pheromones and this activation is partially inhibited in the presence of the male inhibitory pheromone, cis vaccenyl actate (cVA) (Kohatsu et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: P1 neurons receive sensory cues signaling females or males and drive courtship decisions.
source: These data show that P1 neurons receive sensory cues signaling females or males and drive courtship decisions, suggesting that they may be command neurons for courtship behaviors.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited experimental data.

claim: P1 neurons may be command neurons for courtship behaviors.
source: These data show that P1 neurons receive sensory cues signaling females or males and drive courtship decisions, suggesting that they may be command neurons for courtship behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on prior data.

claim: The sensory pathways that converge onto P1 neurons are poorly defined.
source: The sensory pathways that converge onto P1 neurons are poorly defined.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Diverse sensory stimuli contribute to courtship decisions, including visual, auditory, and chemosensory cues.
source: Diverse sensory stimuli contribute to courtship decisions, including visual, auditory, and chemosensory cues.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila courtship.

claim: Sex-specific cuticular hydrocarbons act as pheromones detected primarily by contact chemosensory neurons.
source: Important sensory cues detected primarily by contact chemosensory neurons are sex-specific cuticular hydrocarbons that act as pheromones.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Multiple gustatory receptors and neurons have been implicated in pheromone detection.
source: Multiple gustatory receptors and neurons have been implicated in pheromone detection (Bray and Amrein, 2003; Koh et al., 2014; Miyamoto and Amrein, 2008; Moon et al., 2009; Watanabe et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Leg chemosensory neurons expressing the PPK23 pickpocket ion channel detect pheromones.
source: We and others recently showed that leg chemosensory neurons expressing the PPK23 pickpocket ion channel detect pheromones (Lu et al., 2012; Thistle et al., 2012; Toda et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research including the authors' own work.

claim: PPK23 is expressed in sensory neurons of many leg chemosensory bristles, with generally two PPK23 cells per bristle.
source: PPK23 is expressed in sensory neurons of many leg chemosensory bristles, with generally two PPK23 cells per bristle.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about PPK23 expression pattern.

claim: One PPK23 cell per bristle responds selectively to male pheromones (M cells) and the other cell to female pheromones (F cells).
source: One cell responds selectively to male pheromones (M cells) and the other cell to female pheromones (F cells) (Pikielny, 2012; Thistle et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The PPK25 channel is expressed in one of the two PPK23-positive cells per bristle.
source: In contrast, the PPK25 channel is expressed in one of the two PPK23-positive cells per bristle, and PPK25 is required for cellular and behavioral responses to female pheromones, arguing that it selectively labels F cells (Starostina et al., 2012; Vijayan et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PPK25 is required for cellular and behavioral responses to female pheromones.
source: In contrast, the PPK25 channel is expressed in one of the two PPK23-positive cells per bristle, and PPK25 is required for cellular and behavioral responses to female pheromones, arguing that it selectively labels F cells (Starostina et al., 2012; Vijayan et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PPK25 selectively labels F cells.
source: In contrast, the PPK25 channel is expressed in one of the two PPK23-positive cells per bristle, and PPK25 is required for cellular and behavioral responses to female pheromones, arguing that it selectively labels F cells (Starostina et al., 2012; Vijayan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on cited research about PPK25 expression and function.

claim: PPK23 cells are Fruitless-positive.
source: Unlike other classes of gustatory neurons implicated in pheromone detection, PPK23 cells are Fruitless-positive (Lu et al., 2012; Thistle et al., 2012; Toda et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: F cells (PPK23+ PPK25+) respond to female pheromones whereas M cells (PPK23+ PPK25-) respond to male pheromones.
source: By GCaMP6s calcium imaging (Chen et al., 2013) of PPK23 cells in a background in which PPK25 cells were independently labeled, we first confirmed that the PPK25-positive cells (F cells) are tuned to female pheromones and the PPK25-negative cells (M cells) to male pheromones (Figure 1A,B; Table 1 contains genotypes of flies used for all experiments).
evidence: This is confirmed by calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: F cells are the only leg neurons that express the vesicular glutamate transporter-Gal4 driver (vGlut-Gal4).
source: In addition, we found that F cells are the only leg neurons that express the vesicular glutamate transporter-Gal4 driver (vGlut-Gal4) (Daniels et al., 2008), suggesting that the two classes differ in their neurotransmitter profiles and providing an additional marker that selectively labels F cells (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: F cells and M cells differ in their neurotransmitter profiles.
source: In addition, we found that F cells are the only leg neurons that express the vesicular glutamate transporter-Gal4 driver (vGlut-Gal4) (Daniels et al., 2008), suggesting that the two classes differ in their neurotransmitter profiles and providing an additional marker that selectively labels F cells (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is inferred from the differential expression of vGlut-Gal4.

claim: F cells terminate in the ventral nerve cord (VNC).
source: F cells and M cells also differ in their axonal projection patterns: F cells terminate in the ventral nerve cord (VNC) whereas M cells also have fibers that project to the subesophageal zone (SEZ) of the central brain (Figure 1E,G).
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 1E.

claim: M cells have fibers that project to the subesophageal zone (SEZ) of the central brain.
source: F cells and M cells also differ in their axonal projection patterns: F cells terminate in the ventral nerve cord (VNC) whereas M cells also have fibers that project to the subesophageal zone (SEZ) of the central brain (Figure 1E,G).
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 1G.

claim: Expression of dTRPA1 in F cells promoted male-female courtship upon heat-evoked neural activation.
source: Males expressing dTRPA1 in F cells tested at 30°C (a temperature that activates dTRPA1) had a significantly higher wing extension rate than genetically identical flies tested at the non-activating temperature of 23°C or control flies at either temperature (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Males expressing dTRPA1 in M cells had a significantly lower wing extension rate at 30°C compared to genetic and temperature controls.
source: In contrast, males expressing dTRPA1 in M cells had a significantly lower wing extension rate at 30°C compared to genetic and temperature controls (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 1H.

claim: F and M cells comprise genetically and anatomically distinct chemosensory neuron classes that respond to female or male pheromones and promote or inhibit courtship.
source: Thus, F and M cells comprise genetically and anatomically distinct chemosensory neuron classes that respond to female or male pheromones and promote or inhibit courtship.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Activation of F cells triggered calcium increases in P1.
source: Activation of F cells triggered calcium increases in P1, demonstrating that sensory neurons that detect female pheromones activate courtship-promoting P1 neurons.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 2B.

claim: No significant calcium response was observed in P1 neurons upon M cell activation.
source: In contrast, we observed no significant calcium response in P1 neurons upon M cell activation.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 2B.

claim: Activating F+M cells using the ppk23-LexA driver caused robust calcium responses in P1 neurons.
source: Activating F+M cells using the same ppk23-LexA driver (without expression of Gal80 in F cells) caused robust calcium responses in P1 neurons.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 2B.

claim: F cells, but not M cells, activate P1 neurons.
source: These experiments argue that F cells, but not M cells, activate P1 neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the calcium imaging data in Figure 2B.

claim: PPN1 neurons have cell bodies on the dorsal surface of the third leg neuromere.
source: PPN1 neurons have cell bodies on the dorsal surface of the third leg neuromere, send projections to all leg and wing neuromeres in the VNC, and terminate in the ventrolateral protocerebrum.
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 3A.

claim: PPN1 neurons send projections to all leg and wing neuromeres in the VNC.
source: PPN1 neurons have cell bodies on the dorsal surface of the third leg neuromere, send projections to all leg and wing neuromeres in the VNC, and terminate in the ventrolateral protocerebrum.
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 3A.

claim: PPN1 neurons terminate in the ventrolateral protocerebrum.
source: PPN1 neurons have cell bodies on the dorsal surface of the third leg neuromere, send projections to all leg and wing neuromeres in the VNC, and terminate in the ventrolateral protocerebrum.
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 3A.

claim: PPN1 dendrites are in close proximity to PPK25 axons.
source: PPN1 dendrites are in close proximity to PPK25 axons and PPN1 axons overlap with P1 fibers, as shown by double labeling experiments (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 3E.

claim: PPN1 axons overlap with P1 fibers.
source: PPN1 dendrites are in close proximity to PPK25 axons and PPN1 axons overlap with P1 fibers, as shown by double labeling experiments (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 3F.

claim: Activating PPN1 with dTRPA1 increased male courtship behavior toward females, as measured by unilateral wing extension rate.
source: Consistent with a role in promoting courtship, activating PPN1 with dTRPA1 increased male courtship behavior toward females, as measured by unilateral wing extension rate (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PPN1 is not Fru-positive based on intersectional approaches with Fru-Flp and Fru-LexA.
source: Unlike other neurons of the courtship circuit, PPN1 is not Fru-positive based on intersectional approaches with Fru-Flp and Fru-LexA and PPN1 projections are not sexually dimorphic (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding, though data are not shown.

claim: PPN1 projections are not sexually dimorphic.
source: Unlike other neurons of the courtship circuit, PPN1 is not Fru-positive based on intersectional approaches with Fru-Flp and Fru-LexA and PPN1 projections are not sexually dimorphic (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding, though data are not shown.

claim: F cell stimulation activates PPN1 axons.
source: These studies revealed calcium increases in PPN1 axons upon F cell stimulation but not M cell stimulation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 4A.

claim: M cell stimulation does not activate PPN1 axons.
source: These studies revealed calcium increases in PPN1 axons upon F cell stimulation but not M cell stimulation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 4A.

claim: Activating F+M cells using the ppk23-LexA driver triggered robust calcium responses in PPN1.
source: As with P1, activating F+M cells using the same ppk23-LexA driver (without expression of Gal80 in F cells) triggered robust calcium responses in PPN1, further arguing that PPN1 neurons are downstream of F cells and not M cells.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 4A.

claim: PPN1 neurons are downstream of F cells and not M cells.
source: As with P1, activating F+M cells using the same ppk23-LexA driver (without expression of Gal80 in F cells) triggered robust calcium responses in PPN1, further arguing that PPN1 neurons are downstream of F cells and not M cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the calcium imaging data.

claim: Activation of PPN1 with red light generated calcium responses in P1.
source: Activation of PPN1 with red light generated calcium responses in P1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by optogenetic activation and calcium imaging in Figure 4B.

claim: Female pheromones activate a neural pathway from F cells to PPN1 to P1 to drive courtship behavior.
source: Together, these experiments argue that female pheromones activate a neural pathway from F cells to PPN1 to P1 to drive courtship behavior.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figures 2-4.

claim: mAL neurons are anatomically identifiable by their distinct arborization patterns.
source: These were anatomically identifiable as mAL neurons (a.k.a. aDT2, aDTb) by their distinct arborization patterns (Cachero et al., 2010; Ito et al., 2012; Kimura et al., 2005; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on anatomical characterization supported by citations.

claim: mAL neurons have been proposed to be sexually dimorphic GABAergic interneurons that convey inhibitory courtship signals to the higher brain in males.
source: Based on their anatomy and neurotransmitter profile, mAL neurons have been proposed to be sexually dimorphic GABAergic interneurons that convey inhibitory courtship signals to the higher brain in males (Koganezawa et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a proposal from prior research cited in the manuscript.

claim: R43D01-Gal4 includes Fru-positive, GABAergic mAL neurons.
source: To examine these questions, we visually screened Gal4 lines (Jenett et al., 2012) and identified R43D01-Gal4, which includes Fru-positive, GABAergic mAL neurons (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by anatomical and immunohistochemical characterization in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: M cell axons and mAL dendrites overlap in the SEZ.
source: Consistent with the notion that mAL might be downstream of pheromone-sensing sensory neurons, we found that M cell axons and mAL dendrites overlap in the SEZ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Activating mAL neurons with dTRPA1 suppresses courtship toward females.
source: Activation of mAL neurons with dTRPA1 greatly suppressed courtship toward females compared to controls (Figure 5C), as measured by unilateral wing extension rate.
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Inactivation of mAL neurons with tetanus toxin caused robust male-male chaining.
source: Inactivation of mAL neurons with tetanus toxin caused robust male-male chaining, a behavior in which three or more males serially court each other (Figure 5D), and which was almost never observed in control animals.
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Expression of RNAi against the vesicular GABA transporter (vGAT) using R43D01-Gal4 caused male-male chaining.
source: Furthermore, expression of RNAi against the vesicular GABA transporter (vGAT) using R43D01-Gal4 also caused male-male chaining (Figure 5D), arguing that GABA release from mAL inhibits courtship.
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 5D.

claim: GABA release from mAL inhibits courtship.
source: Furthermore, expression of RNAi against the vesicular GABA transporter (vGAT) using R43D01-Gal4 also caused male-male chaining (Figure 5D), arguing that GABA release from mAL inhibits courtship.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data in Figure 5D.

claim: Activation of mAL inhibits courtship.
source: Thus, activation of mAL inhibits courtship, whereas inactivation enhances courtship, demonstrating an inhibitory role for mAL in courtship decisions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral experiments.

claim: Inactivation of mAL enhances courtship.
source: Thus, activation of mAL inhibits courtship, whereas inactivation enhances courtship, demonstrating an inhibitory role for mAL in courtship decisions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral experiments.

claim: Both M cells and F cells activated mAL.
source: Surprisingly, both M cells and F cells activated mAL, arguing that detection of female as well as male pheromones provides an inhibitory courtship drive.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 5E,F.

claim: Detection of female as well as male pheromones provides an inhibitory courtship drive.
source: Surprisingly, both M cells and F cells activated mAL, arguing that detection of female as well as male pheromones provides an inhibitory courtship drive.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the calcium imaging data.

claim: F cells additionally activated PPN1 and P1 courtship-promoting neurons, whereas M cells did not.
source: As F cells additionally activated PPN1 and P1 courtship-promoting neurons, whereas M cells did not, this suggests that the balance between excitation and inhibition underlies the decision to court.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from earlier experiments.

claim: The balance between excitation and inhibition underlies the decision to court.
source: As F cells additionally activated PPN1 and P1 courtship-promoting neurons, whereas M cells did not, this suggests that the balance between excitation and inhibition underlies the decision to court.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: P1 neurons are in close proximity to mAL termini.
source: P1 neurons are in close proximity to mAL termini (Figure 6A), suggesting that they may be candidate targets of GABAergic mAL neurons.
evidence: This is shown by anatomical imaging in Figure 6A.

claim: P1 neurons may be candidate targets of GABAergic mAL neurons.
source: P1 neurons are in close proximity to mAL termini (Figure 6A), suggesting that they may be candidate targets of GABAergic mAL neurons.
evidence: This is a speculation based on anatomical proximity.

claim: Males expressing Rdl RNAi in P1 neurons displayed increased courtship toward other males.
source: Males expressing Rdl RNAi in P1 neurons displayed increased courtship toward other males, arguing that P1 neurons receive GABAergic inhibition (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 6B.

claim: P1 neurons receive GABAergic inhibition.
source: Males expressing Rdl RNAi in P1 neurons displayed increased courtship toward other males, arguing that P1 neurons receive GABAergic inhibition (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data in Figure 6B.

claim: Chrimson-mediated activation of P1 neurons induced courtship behavior in solitary males.
source: In addition, whereas Chrimson-mediated activation of P1 neurons induced courtship behavior in solitary males, co-activation of P1 and R43D01-Gal4 neurons suppressed this behavior (Figure 6C), arguing that mAL suppresses P1-mediated courtship.
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Co-activation of P1 and R43D01-Gal4 neurons suppressed courtship behavior in solitary males.
source: In addition, whereas Chrimson-mediated activation of P1 neurons induced courtship behavior in solitary males, co-activation of P1 and R43D01-Gal4 neurons suppressed this behavior (Figure 6C), arguing that mAL suppresses P1-mediated courtship.
evidence: This is a behavioral finding shown in Figure 6C.

claim: mAL suppresses P1-mediated courtship.
source: In addition, whereas Chrimson-mediated activation of P1 neurons induced courtship behavior in solitary males, co-activation of P1 and R43D01-Gal4 neurons suppressed this behavior (Figure 6C), arguing that mAL suppresses P1-mediated courtship.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data in Figure 6C.

claim: Simultaneous stimulation of F and M cells caused transient activation of P1.
source: Indeed, simultaneous stimulation of F and M cells caused transient activation of P1 and lesioning mAL axons significantly increased P1 activation.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 6D.

claim: Lesioning mAL axons significantly increased P1 activation upon simultaneous stimulation of F and M cells.
source: Indeed, simultaneous stimulation of F and M cells caused transient activation of P1 and lesioning mAL axons significantly increased P1 activation.
evidence: This is shown by calcium imaging experiments in Figure 6D.

claim: mAL neurons inhibit P1 neurons via GABA-A receptors.
source: These data suggest that mAL neurons inhibit P1 neurons via GABA-A receptors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Chrimson-mediated activation of mAL neurons evoked a rapid increase in ArcLight fluorescence in P1 neurons, indicating hyperpolarization.
source: Chrimson-mediated activation of mAL neurons, using R43D01-LexA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), evoked a rapid increase in ArcLight fluorescence in P1 neurons, indicating hyperpolarization.
evidence: This is shown by voltage imaging experiments in Figure 6E,F.

claim: mAL neurons provide an inhibitory drive onto P1 neurons.
source: These experiments demonstrate that mAL neurons provide an inhibitory drive onto P1 neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Female pheromones trigger neural pathways that excite and inhibit P1.
source: Female pheromones trigger neural pathways that excite and inhibit P1, with PPN1 providing an excitatory drive onto P1 and mAL providing an inhibitory drive.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: PPN1 provides an excitatory drive onto P1.
source: Female pheromones trigger neural pathways that excite and inhibit P1, with PPN1 providing an excitatory drive onto P1 and mAL providing an inhibitory drive.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: mAL provides an inhibitory drive onto P1.
source: Female pheromones trigger neural pathways that excite and inhibit P1, with PPN1 providing an excitatory drive onto P1 and mAL providing an inhibitory drive.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

source: Taken together, these studies reveal an elegant strategy used by the nervous system in which excitatory and inhibitory inputs directly converge onto a common output to control a significant behavioral decision.

claim: Ablating F cells using diphtheria toxin leaves M cells intact, with one GFP-positive cell per bristle rather than two.

claim: A recent study identified vAB3 neurons as activated by female but not male pheromones.
source: Indeed, a recent study identified vAB3 neurons, with projections in the first leg neuromere in the VNC, the SEZ and protocerebrum, as activated by female but not male pheromones (Clowney et al., 2015).

evidence: This statement is supported by reference to a recent study (Clowney et al., 2015).
